**ID:** Ja 110  
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sabbasaṁhārakapañhajātaka* (also attested as *Sabbasamhārakapañha*, Ja 110) is a canonical text within the Pali Jātaka collection, situated as the tenth and concluding discourse of the eleventh chapter, the *Parosatavagga* [Fausböll 1877].

Rather than presenting a standalone narrative at this place in the canon, the text serves as an abbreviated pointer or cross-reference. Opening with the phrase “There is no All-embracing” (*Sabbasaṁhārako natthi*), it states that this All-embracing Question will be expounded in all its aspects at length in the *Ummaggajātaka* (Ja 546) [Fausböll 1877]. Following this notice, the text concludes both the question itself and the *Parosatavagga* [Fausböll 1877].
